output.reasoning_summary:
After investigating potential challenges to the initial verdict, I found:

H1 (Restatements): No relevant evidence was found regarding any restatements, corrections, or adjustments to the reported net operating revenues for Q3 2026 or Q3 2025.

H2 (Different number of days): This challenge is REFUTED. While the evidence confirms that quarters end on the Friday closest to the last day of the corresponding quarterly calendar period (E1, E6), and Q3 2026 ended October 2, 2026 while Q3 2025 ended September 26, 2025, both quarters represent standard three-month periods. The evidence from the original packet (E1) noted that the first quarter of 2026 had six additional days compared to Q1 2025, but this does not apply to Q3. The quarters are comparable for revenue comparison purposes.

H3 (Acquisitions/divestitures): This challenge is REFUTED. While E5 confirms there were some structural changes (India refranchising in May 2025 and Nigeria sale in October 2025), E11 shows that acquisitions and divestitures had only a -1% impact on the consolidated 7% revenue growth for Q3 2026. The vast majority of the 7% increase came from volume (7%), price/mix (1%), and foreign currency (1%). The claim does not assert that the increase was organic or exclude structural changes—it simply states that revenues increased year over year, which is factually correct.

The initial verdict of SUPPORTED remains correct. The evidence clearly establishes that net operating revenues for Q3 2026 ($13,380 million) increased compared to Q3 2025 ($12,455 million), representing a 7% or $925 million increase.
